Round 6's fifteen review findings, and the two the reviewer raised outside the threads. The two critical ones were each a round that could never end rightly: a retired or failed claim kept its round, so the sweep read it against the replacement pod and wrote the data-loss message on the issue every minute; and every ask of a round carried the same delivery id, which the shim's own dedupe (internal/shimwire/dedupe.go) answers locally once that turn has ended, so the worker most in need of a re-task got nothing while the daemon confirmed the task and reset its clock. Each of the fifteen is answered in a resolved thread of sjawhar/legion#2538 with the test that holds it. Two rules behind them are worth carrying: a decision read from a claim with no running process — its recorded plugin contract, its absent locator — is not a decision about a process; and a round that waits must have something that tells somebody when the wait never ends.

The reviewer's two findings outside the threads. A worker whose jj cannot answer refused its own signal, although the head is optional and the daemon verifies none of it, so a stale lock or a recreated workspace could hold a round open until an operator drained the pod; the signal now goes without the head, and the answer carries jj's own message so the worker can repair it. And the issue's acceptance wants a test per touched package that fails on main: two of the five needed care to be honest, because the daemon's round tests and the contracts schema test cannot compile at main at all, and the pull request says which substitute was run and why.

Round 4's defect, found by the tester: a pod that no round covers was replaced by neither its launch nor a round. PodDrift answers nothing for the project controller's pod — it has no issue workspace and nothing to push, so there is nobody to ask and no disk to protect — while rounds 1 and 2 had taken image and pod-shape drift out of the launch's replace decision for every pod, and three facets out of movedInPod for every role. Eight cells of the table below therefore read 'neither': the controller would have run for ever in the pod it was created in, with no broker, so the token its slack_post is granted never reaches it, with none of the files role_config_files.controller names, and writing its session against the store that pod projects — and nothing said so, because the round-2 fix had made the start command itself consistent with the old pod. One predicate, roundCovers(kind), now answers both sides.

The table the architect asked for, read from the code and from runs. Each kind of drift, who replaces the pod, and the test that holds it. An issue pod: image, the kind's reservation, operator volumes, operator mounts and the disk size are the round's (TestPodDriftNamesEachConfigurationKeyThatMoved, TestALaunchKeepsAnIssuePodWhateverOfItsShapeMoved, TestRelaunchKeepsADriftedPodAndReplacesASuspendedSandboxs); the role overlays, the broker enrollment and the session store are the round's (TestPodDriftReadsTheFacetsThatAreNoLongerStaleAddresses, TestEvaluateReadsAPodStaleExactlyWhenRelaunchReplacesIt, TestAddingARoleOverlaysMountDriftsAnIssuePodMadeWithoutIt, TestAPodUnderAnotherSessionStoreHasDrifted); the pod layout and the worker stream are the launch's (TestAnIssuePodOfTheEarlierLayoutIsStaleForEveryRoleAndReplacedByTheNextLaunch, TestEvaluateReadsAPodStaleExactlyWhenRelaunchReplacesIt). A pod no round covers: every one of those ten is the launch's (TestALaunchReplacesAPodNoRoundCoversWhoseShapeHasDrifted for the five shape keys, TestTheControllersPodIsNotLeftBehindByAConfigurationItCannotCarry for the three facets, TestRelaunchKeepsADriftedPodAndReplacesASuspendedSandboxs for its image row; the layout is an issue pod's shape alone and the stream is the same kind-independent branch of movedInPod). The readers of those three predicates, so a later change can find them: relaunch (movedInPod per role, and shapeDrift for a pod no round covers), verdict (movedInPod, which is what makes such a pod read StaleAddress), PodDrift (driftedInPod and shapeDrift, nil when roundCovers is false), the daemon's groupDrift and reconcilePodUpdates (PodDrift per claim, grouped by issue, and independently skipping a claim with no issue, so the daemon's own grouping agrees with the predicate), and the fake and tmux runtimes, which script it and answer nil.

Round 3's defect, found by the tester and swept by the architect's order: the enrollment decision was in four places. The argv read the launch's own enrolls, while the environment (AGENT_SECRETS_URL, AGENT_SECRETS_KEY_DIR), the Sandbox's address record and the observation that compares it each read r.agentSecrets alone. The environment told a role it held a broker whose key directory its pod does not mount, which skill://legion-worker has a role act on before it reports a resource unreachable; and the record claimed an address that generation never had, which a later move of the broker's URL would read as a stale address and replace the process mid-turn. There is now one predicate, Runtime.enrollsIn(pod, role), read by all four. The launch reads it of the kept pod's stored template and an observation of the live pod; they agree because nothing takes a volume off a running pod, which is written into that predicate's doc.

A sweep cannot rebuild the pod template a launch would build: r.podTemplate(l) takes a launch whose gh projection is keyed off freshly minted GitHub App tokens (relaunch.go gitHubBundles), so a sweep that rebuilt it would mint credentials for every pod every minute. The launch therefore records the configuration it built from, as the legion.dev/pod-shape annotation in the pod template's own metadata, written by the existing podTemplate build and carried by the existing /spec/podTemplate patch — no new write site.

Drift is read from the stored Sandbox's template, never the pod: GKE Autopilot rewrites a pod's requirements at admission, which is why the repository cache's own check (templateResized) reads the template too.

The annotation's JSON must be canonical or two equal configurations compare different and every pod of the fleet reads as drifted at once. The record has a fixed field order, Go sorts a ResourceList's map keys and a resource.Quantity marshals as its own canonical string; TestPodShapeEncodesEqualConfigurationsIdentically holds it to that, and quantities are compared by amount so 1024Mi and 1Gi are no drift.

A suspended claim has no Locator (machine.go's letGo clears it), so the round groups claims by issue rather than by locator — otherwise the spec's 'suspended ones included' could not hold. A claim blocks the round when it has a session and is not retired; a claim with no session has never had a worker and blocks nothing.

A worker answers ready_for_update from inside a turn, so the round completes only when no claim of the group is in StateWorking. That is what keeps the promise that no worker is stopped mid-turn; the same condition ends a plugin round.

ReplacePod only suspends the Sandbox naming the displaced pod and waits the pod out. It provisions nothing: the existing displaced path resumes every role uncharged on its own session, and the first of those resumes finds the Sandbox suspended and provisions a fresh pod from the current template — today's path, unchanged, and no suspension of a role was added.

The simplify pass measured PodDrift at 498 us and 914 allocations per call because storedSandbox decoded the whole Sandbox to read one annotation; the sweep makes that call per claim per minute for the whole deployment. It now reads the annotation off the undecoded store object and decodes only when it differs: 6.1 us and 17 allocations. The two kinds' shapes are encoded once at construction.

The same pass found PodUpdateSignalled was not fenced: api.readyForUpdate requires generation and sessionId, but Machine.fence had no case for the event, so a process of a superseded generation could end a round. That is now fenced as every other claim request is — the one behavioural change the pass made, with TestPodUpdateSignalIsFenced to hold it.

Round 2's defect, found by the tester: the three facets that became drift are not only configuration the pod carries, they are configuration the role's own start command is built from. A kept pod lacking the broker's enrollment or a role's overlay was still handed a start naming both, so the shim exited 1 or Oh My Pi refused to start, the claim never registered, and the round that must replace that pod was blocked by the pod itself — an operator drain being the only way out, which is the outage this issue exists to end. The fix is the architect's: build a kept pod's start from that pod's stored Sandbox template, leave out what it cannot carry, let the role run degraded until the round replaces it, and replace the pod at the launch when the template cannot be read.
deviations: D3 of the plan ends a round with 'RequestSuspend{By: daemon} to each asked claim → ReplacePod → a start outbox row per claim'. This implementation calls ReplacePod alone, with no suspension and no start rows, which is D3's own first paragraph ('each worker is then resumed by the existing rule path'). Suspending each claim would strand it, because a suspended claim is resumed by nothing on its own; the displaced path already resumes every role uncharged and provisions the new pod. INFRA-714's architect also asked on 2026-10-29 that no suspension of a role be added while its issue is open, and this shape adds none.

D6 says a claim blocks the round 'unless it is retired'. A claim with no session is excluded too: it has never had a worker, so it holds nothing unpushed, and with the by-issue grouping that D6's own 'claims whose Locator names the pod' excluded it as well. failed and operator-suspended claims still block, with the update-stalled notice as the consequence, exactly as D6 says.

The round's identity is 'pod:<pod uid>' rather than a minted token, so the sweep can tell from the claim's own column which pod the round was opened for and write the issue's message when that pod went without the round completing.

discoveredComplexity: movedInPod was wider than its name: three of its five facets (movedRoleOverlays, movedEnrollment, movedSessionStore) are volumes and mounts, which R9 reads as drift, while the root spec's reason for exempting StaleAddress — the worker cannot reach the daemon — holds only for movedStream and movedLayout. The split follows that stated reason; INFRA-714's architect confirmed it on the issue. A consequence stated plainly: a launch into a pod that lacks the broker's volumes or a role overlay now starts the role in that pod rather than replacing it, and only the round fixes it.

A claim holds at most one pending delivery, so the update task could have displaced a phase task. It does not: the task has a round-stable id, a claim already holding a phase task is refused ErrDeliveryPending — which the machine treats as a wait — and the minute sweep lands the task as soon as that turn ends.
